en.title: Maria Sten Steps Out of Reacher's Shadow for Her Own Chicago Conspiracy
en.summary: Frances Neagley, the formidable private investigator from 'Reacher,' gets her own Prime Video series. Star Maria Sten discusses stepping into the spotlight and what fans can expect from the new show.
en.body:
For three seasons, **Maria Sten** has been the formidable force of nature known as Frances Neagley, the no-nonsense private investigator and loyal companion to Alan Ritchson's Jack Reacher. Now, she’s stepping into her own spotlight with the highly anticipated Prime Video spin-off, simply titled **“Neagley.”** The series, which premiered on September 16, 2026, sees Neagley trading Reacher's nomadic lifestyle for a permanent base of operations as a private eye in Chicago. This new venture isn't just about expanding her role; it's about exploring the depths of a character who has quickly become a fan favorite.

"Neagley" centers on the titular character as she's drawn into a dangerous conspiracy following the mysterious death of a childhood friend. Armed with the combat skills honed during her military career and her time alongside Reacher, Neagley must navigate the gritty streets of Chicago. She’s not alone, however, as she teams up with a conflicted local cop, **Greyston Holt's** Hudson Riley, a streetwise kid named Keno, and her own protégé, **Adeline Rudolph's** Renee Birdwhistle. This ensemble promises to bring a dynamic new energy to the unfolding mystery, allowing Neagley to showcase her investigative acumen as much as her fighting prowess.

## Unpacking the 'Neagley' Phenomenon

Stepping into a lead role after being a key supporting player comes with its own set of challenges, and **Maria Sten** is ready for them. The series promises to delve deeper into Neagley's past and motivations, offering audiences a more intimate look at the woman behind the tactical gear. The official trailer teases a thrilling narrative where Neagley’s pursuit of justice for her fallen friend becomes a relentless quest against a menacing evil. Her military background and her training under Jack Reacher have clearly prepared her for this moment, but the personal stakes in **“Neagley”** raise the intensity to a new level. The show aims to reveal not just the fighter, but the person Neagley is when she’s the one calling the shots.

## The Fan Connection

Fans of **“Reacher”** have long clamored for more of Frances Neagley, drawn to her quiet competence, unwavering loyalty, and impressive combat skills that often rival Reacher’s own. The announcement of a dedicated spin-off was met with widespread excitement, signaling a significant expansion of the beloved Prime Video universe. The premise of **“Neagley”**—a complex conspiracy rooted in personal loss—is sure to resonate with viewers who appreciate well-crafted crime dramas with compelling character arcs. The series’ move to Chicago also provides a distinct setting that will shape the narrative, offering a different flavor than the episodic, small-town adventures of **“Reacher.”** The anticipation is palpable for a show that promises to be as action-packed as it is character-driven.

## What's Next

**“Neagley”** is now available to stream, with all episodes of its first season released simultaneously on September 16, 2026, on Prime Video. Viewers can expect a full season of investigations, action, and character development as Frances Neagley carves out her own path in the world of private investigation.

content_raw: Danish-Congolese actor and Maria Sten has some big shoes to fill (literally). Granted, she’s spent three seasons on Prime Video’s hit action series “ Reacher ” playing no-nonsense private investigator Frances Neagley, frequent ringer and closest companion to Alan Ritchson’s itinerant titan Jack Reacher. She’s a fellow MP and compatriot who can throw down just as easily as Reacher can with half of Ritchson’s bulk, and her appearances in the flagship show have made her a household favorite. But in the upcoming spinoff “Neagley,” it’s her show through and through, which comes with no small amount of pressure. Where each season of “Reacher” sees its bulky problem-solver in a new town, a new dilemma, and with a new supporting cast, “Neagley”‘s home is in Chicago, where she’s set up shop as a private eye. And this season uses the mysterious death of a childhood friend of Neagley’s to force her into uncovering a broader conspiracy, with the help of a conflicted Chicago cop (Greyston Holt’s Hudson Riley), a streetwise kid (Jasper Jones’ Keno), and her protege at her PI firm (“ Mortal Kombat II ” alum Adeline Rudolph as Renee Birdwhistle). In the week prior to the show’s release, Sten sat down with RogerEbert.com during a press junket in Chicago (hours before Sten was to catch the seventh-inning stretch at Wrigley Field) to talk about expanding her role into a full-length series, the training required for such a show, and what the new series will teach us about Neagley as a person and a fighter. This interview has been edited for length and clarity. You’ve been playing Neagley since 2022, and the character’s been a big hit since the first season of “Reacher.” What were the first rumblings of a possibility that Neagley could sustain herself as the center of a spinoff? Interestingly enough, that came up when I first booked the job. If it went well, and it was a success, we thought there might be a possibility of a Neagley spinoff. I thought, “Right, of course, because that happens, sure.” But I’m just so surprised we’re finally here, because I didn’t feel that was necessarily in the cards. Reacher is very much Reacher, and Neagley comes in to help him out, as is true in the books. But I’m so thrilled to be able to take her on her own little journey. Even when I read the books she’s in, I felt she had so much more hidden under the surface. So I’m excited we’re finally getting to see all of that now. Yes, because Neagley hasn’t been the central focus of a Lee Child book to date, and all the “Reacher” seasons are based on a specific book. What were the challenges you guys had in building on that source material to craft more layers for her to delve into? We have freedom in the sense that there is no specific book to work off.
